text: Define a proposition.

text: Define a truth table.

points.text: A table of a logical expression’s value, for every combination of its inputs.

text: Define a compound proposition.

points.text: A proposition made of simpler ones, joined by connectives.

subject: computerscience
text: Define a connective.

points.text: A symbol that joins propositions, such as ∧, ∨, ~, ⇒ and ⇔.

text: Define conjunction.

points.text: The proposition p ∧ q, true only when both p and q are true.

subject: computerscience
text: Define disjunction.

points.text: The proposition p ∨ q, false only when both p and q are false.

subject: computerscience
text: Define negation.

points.text: The proposition ~p, with the opposite truth value to p.

subject: computerscience
text: Define a conditional.

points.text: The proposition p ⇒ q, false only when p is true and q is false.

subject: computerscience
text: Define a biconditional.

points.text: The proposition p ⇔ q, true when p and q have the same truth value.

subject: computerscience
text: Define a contradiction.

points.text: A formula that’s false for every assignment of truth values.

subject: computerscience
text: Define a well-formed formula.

points.text: A formula built correctly from variables, connectives and brackets.

subject: computerscience
text: Define an atomic proposition.

points.text: A proposition that can’t be split into simpler propositions.

subject: computerscience
text: A lift’s motor should run when both A and B are true, where A and B are statements read from two sensors. (i) Which connective joins A and B to give this? (ii) Give a reason.

points.text: (i) ∧, the conjunction A ∧ B.
(ii) A ∧ B is true only when both A and B are true.

subject: computerscience
text: A lift’s motor should run when at least one of A and B is true, where A and B are statements read from two sensors. (i) Which connective joins A and B to give this? (ii) Give a reason.

points.text: (i) ∨, the disjunction A ∨ B.
(ii) A ∨ B is false only when both A and B are false.

subject: computerscience
text: A lift’s motor should run when A and B are both true or both false, where A and B are statements read from two sensors. (i) Which connective joins A and B to give this? (ii) Give a reason.

points.text: (i) ⇔, the biconditional A ⇔ B.
(ii) A ⇔ B is true exactly when A and B have the same truth value.

subject: computerscience
text: A lift’s motor should run when it isn’t the case that A is true and B is false, where A and B are statements read from two sensors. (i) Which connective joins A and B to give this? (ii) Give a reason.

points.text: (i) ⇒, the conditional A ⇒ B.
(ii) A ⇒ B is false only when A is true and B is false.
